standard_prerequisites.name: Description of extension by zero and its stalks
standard_prerequisites.use: Characterizes extension by zero by the vanishing of its stalks outside the open and by its restriction.

standard_prerequisites.name: Pushforward commutes with base change for finite morphisms

core_obligations: Check vanishing of the stalks outside the open (proof lines 11626-11633): at a geometric point of the target outside the open, the stalk of the composite computed by the finite pushforward formula is a sum of stalks of the extension by zero at points outside the open, hence zero.

Identify the restriction to the open (proof lines 11634-11638): restricting the composite along the open immersion gives the pushforward of the original sheaf, by base change compatibility and the description of the extension by zero.
Conclude (proof lines 11638-11648): the two properties characterize extension by zero, so the two composites agree; the author notes that functoriality in the sheaf is a routine verification.
proof_roadmap: Compute the stalks of both sides outside the open subset and see that they vanish.
Compute the restrictions of both sides to the open subset and identify them.
Use the characterization of extension by zero and record functoriality.
difficulty_reason: The lemma is the base change compatibility f_* of extension by zero equals extension by zero of g_* for a cartesian square with f finite and j an open immersion (statement lines 11611-11623). The proof is a complete stalk computation: the stems of the composite pushforward are computed by the finite pushforward formula and vanish at geometric points outside the open (proof lines 11626-11633); the restriction to the open is identified by base change compatibility together with the description of extension by zero (proof lines 11634-11638); and the characterization of extension by zero then forces the two functors to agree (proof lines 11638-11648). The non-formal content is the two computations. The claim is H2: a written stalk computation followed by a characterization.
